ground_truth_witness: Let S₁=S₂=S₃={0<1}, the two-element frame, and let φ:S₁→S₂ be the identity. Its restriction to S₁×S₃ is unchanged. φ preserves top, finite meets, and all joins, so it is a frame homomorphism. Take A={0,1}. Then ∨₁A=1 and φ[A]={0,1}.
ground_truth_flaw: The arbitrary-join calculation claims that φ(∨₁A) = ∧₂φ[A].
